newsitem.title: USA: PSE&G allowed to expand appliance service business.
newsitem.headline: PSE&G allowed to expand appliance service business.

text.p: Public Service Electric and Gas Co said Thursday its proposal to expand its appliance service contracts business has been approved by New Jersey's Board of Public Utilities.
The Public Service Enterprise Group Inc subsidiary estimates it will at least triple this business in five years once utilities are deregulated in New Jersey, spokesman Paul Lief Rosengren said.
This business is currently about $25 to $30 million a year, he noted.

The regulators Wednesday approved PSE&G's plans to offer new service contract products and broaden the range of those contracts to include coverage of central air conditioning, dryers and ranges, the utility said.

The approval allows PSE&G to enter into competition with competitors such as Sears, Roebuck and Co, General Electric Co and others who have targeted the roughly $1 billion New Jersey appliance service market, it added.

As a result of the decision, PSE&G announced three service contract options positioned to be less expensive and more encompassing than service contracts offered by manufacturers and other competitors:
-- The "Comfort & Appliance" package includes repair service on a home's central air conditioner, dryer, range with oven and central gas and water heater, for $189.85 per year;
-- The "Comfort" package offers repair on central cooling and gas heating systems for $122.35 per year;
-- The "Heater and Appliance" package covers central gas and water heaters, as well as dryers and ranges with ovens, for $114.25 per year.
